headline: Church 2012 is a density and history reference, not an accuracy target. It recovered 5.27 Mbit with 10 bit errors, no error-correcting code, and about 3000x read coverage. Codecs that combine an outer Reed-Solomon or fountain code with read clustering recover data exactly at far lower coverage and higher error rates.

church_reference.oligo: 159 nt = 96 nt data + 19 nt address + 2 x 22 nt primers
church_reference.errors: 10 bit errors, mostly in homopolymer runs at oligo ends with single coverage
church_reference.ecc: none (redundancy came from many physical copies)

codecs.name: Church et al. 2012
codecs.reported_result: 10 bit errors in 5.27 Mbit at ~3000x coverage

source.title: Next-generation digital information storage in DNA (Science)

codecs.name: Goldman et al. 2013
codecs.reported_result: 739 kB reconstructed with 100% accuracy; one file needed manual correction
codecs.vs_church: Exact recovery, but in the 2026 benchmark it failed to decode under low-fidelity synthesis

source.title: Towards practical, high-capacity, low-maintenance information storage in synthesized DNA (Nature)

codecs.name: Grass et al. 2015 / DNA-RS (Heckel)
codecs.platform_status: simplified (RS outer + CRC inner, not the original inner RS)
codecs.reported_result: Text retrieved error-free after accelerated aging at 60-70 C for up to a month in silica
codecs.vs_church: Better: error-free with an explicit code. DNA-RS was a top performer in the 2026 benchmark, best under low-fidelity synthesis

source.title: ETH Zurich press release on Grass et al. 2015 (EurekAlert)

codecs.name: DNA Fountain (Erlich & Zielinski 2017)
codecs.ecc: LT fountain code + per-droplet check, GC/homopolymer screening
codecs.reported_result: High density; volatile recovery above ~1.7% sequence loss (Ping et al. 2022)
codecs.vs_church: Denser; failed to decode in the 2026 low-fidelity scenario

source.title: DNA Fountain enables a robust and efficient storage architecture (Science)

codecs.name: Organick et al. 2018 (random access)
codecs.reported_result: 200 MB, 35 files, >13 million oligos, each file recovered with no errors via primer-based random access
codecs.vs_church: Far larger scale, error-free, random access

source.title: Random access in large-scale DNA data storage (Nature Biotechnology)

codecs.name: HEDGES (Press et al. 2020)
codecs.ecc: Hash-based inner code correcting indels + outer RS
codecs.reported_result: Corrects up to ~10% nucleotide errors at low code rates; 7.7% basic error tolerance in the 2026 benchmark, weaker on dropout

source.title: An Indel-Resistant Error-Correcting Code for DNA-Based Information Storage (arXiv)

codecs.name: Yin-Yang codec (Ping et al. 2022)
codecs.ecc: Relies on outer code / redundancy; constraint screening
codecs.reported_result: 99.9% recovery above 10^4 molecule copies, ~71% at 10^2 copies
codecs.vs_church: Denser and constraint-compliant; failed in the 2026 low-fidelity scenario

source.title: Towards practical and robust DNA-based data archiving using the yin-yang codec system (Nature Computational Science)

codecs.name: DNA-Aeon (Welzel et al. 2023)
codecs.ecc: Arithmetic-coding inner code + Raptor fountain outer code
codecs.reported_result: 100% decoding up to 7% substitution and 6.5% mixed error rates; 4.8 KB file in 33,516 nt vs 53,550 (HEDGES) and 84,134 (Grass)
codecs.vs_church: Best overall in the 2026 six-codec benchmark alongside DNA-RS

source.title: DNA-Aeon provides flexible arithmetic coding for constraint adherence and error correction (Nature Communications)

codecs.name: Gungnir (2026)
codecs.reported_result: Page could not be read (rate-limited); listed by title only

source.title: Gungnir codec enabling high error-tolerance and low-redundancy DNA storage (Nature Communications)

benchmark_2026.title: Comparison of state-of-the-art error-correction coding for sequence-based DNA data storage (Gimpel et al., Nature Communications, March 2026)
findings: Six codecs compared: DNA-Aeon, DNA Fountain, DNA-RS, Goldman, HEDGES, Yin-Yang, in silico and in vitro.
Codecs tolerated up to 14% errors and 65% sequence loss in isolation.
DNA-Aeon and DNA-RS were the strongest overall; DNA-RS was best under low-fidelity synthesis.
DNA Fountain, Goldman and Yin-Yang could not decode in the low-fidelity (1.5% error) scenario.
Read clustering improved every codec, more than doubling error tolerance.

related_platforms.name: DT4DDS (ETH Zurich)
related_platforms.what: Open-source digital twin of the DNA storage workflow, built from 40 sequencing experiments; models synthesis, PCR, decay and Illumina errors; has a web front-end.

related_platforms.name: UNACORM (arXiv 2608.09673, Aug 2026)
related_platforms.what: Web app benchmarking 8 codecs on density, recovery, runtime and cost; finds no single codec optimal. Reimplemented codecs not validated against originals.

channel_presets.name: Low-fidelity (DT4DDS-informed)
channel_presets.note: Electrochemical synthesis ~13.5e-3 errors/nt, deletion-dominated; the ins/del split is our assumption

channel_presets.name: Stress 5%
channel_presets.note: Synthetic stress test, not a measured channel
